# Tynkr Tools & Co — Desktop App Suite

> Five local-first desktop apps for Windows — Ledger, Vault, Hearth, Forge, and Inkpress. Ordinary files on your PC; no cloud, accounts, or fees.

Tynkr is the desktop software line from Built by Josh Studio LLC, under its Tynkr Tools & Co brand. Each app stores your work in ordinary files on your own machine — open them, move them, or back them up yourself. None of the apps send us your data, and there are no accounts, telemetry, or analytics. The suite is in development and coming soon to the Microsoft Store; visitors can request launch notifications on Substack.

## About & Authority

- **Publisher:** Built by Josh Studio LLC (Kansas Business ID 10076138, Kansas), publishing desktop applications under the **Tynkr Tools & Co** brand.
- **Canonical Site:** https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/
- **Parent Catalog:** https://builtbyjoshstudio.com/ ([llms.txt](https://builtbyjoshstudio.com/llms.txt))
- **Support Email:** support@builtbyjoshstudio.com
- **Pay-Once Model:** Every app is a one-time purchase through the Microsoft Store when it launches. Bug fixes are always free; major version upgrades are a separate purchase. There are no subscriptions, no accounts, and no recurring billing.
- **Architecture & Network Distinction:**
  - **Tynkr Ledger, Vault, Hearth, and Forge:** 100% offline Windows desktop apps that make zero network calls of their own (Microsoft handles Store purchase, licensing, and updates). Data is stored in ordinary JSON / Markdown files in a folder you choose, with optional password encryption on disk.
  - **Tynkr Inkpress:** Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later (x64) desktop app with no account, telemetry, or analytics sent to us. Its own code makes no network calls except downloading remote web-linked images during print PDF export (use local images to avoid any connection); it uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 (which includes SmartScreen) and Edge or Chrome for print PDF export. Files in `Documents\Tynkr Inkpress` and per-book `.inkpress.json` sidecars are not encrypted (protected by your Windows account).

This site (`tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com`) covers the desktop apps only. Broader studio products (Notion OS templates, Excel/Google Sheets workbooks, guided print planners, zodiac art, books, and cookbook) live at `builtbyjoshstudio.com`. Summary index: https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/llms.txt.

## The apps

- [Tynkr Ledger — Personal Finance OS](https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/ledger/): Personal finance on your own disk: transactions, budgets, bills, debt payoff, net worth. Local-first Windows app — no cloud, no accounts, no subscription.
- [Tynkr Vault — Second Brain OS](https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/vault/): Notes in plain Markdown files you own, with tasks, weekly reviews, and typo-tolerant search. Local-first Windows app — no cloud or subscription.
- [Tynkr Hearth — Homebuyer OS](https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/hearth/): Map your home purchase on your own PC: mortgage math, loan comparison, cash-to-close, roadmap, and document checklist. Local-first Windows app.
- [Tynkr Forge — Small Business OS](https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/forge/): Inventory, orders and invoicing for a small shop, with no monthly fee — one local-first Windows app. No cloud, no accounts, no subscription. Features, in order: inventory with stock levels and reorder targets, vendors and purchase orders, customer CRM and sales pipeline, proposals, PDF invoices, projects and time tracking, financial dashboard, contracts, expenses with receipts, and reminders.
- [Tynkr Inkpress — Book Formatting](https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/inkpress/): Format manuscripts into EPUB 3 ebooks, KDP paperback print PDFs, and author-site web pages with live previews. Local-first Windows desktop app with Clean, Styled, and three framed editions (Ashveil, Systemfall, Sootline).

## Suite FAQs

Q: How does pricing work across the Tynkr desktop apps?
A: Every Tynkr app uses a pay-once model — a one-time purchase per app through the Microsoft Store when it launches. Bug fixes are always free, major version upgrades are a separate purchase, and there are no subscriptions, no accounts, and no in-app upgrades.
Q: Where will the Tynkr apps be available, and when do they launch?
A: All five Tynkr apps are in development and coming soon for Windows. They will be certified, signed, sold, and delivered only through the Microsoft Store, with updates delivered automatically through the Store. You can join the Tynkr Tools & Co Substack list below for launch notifications.
Q: Do the Tynkr apps work offline or send data over the internet?
A: None of the five apps have accounts, telemetry, or analytics, and none send your data to Built by Josh Studio LLC. Tynkr Ledger, Vault, Hearth, and Forge make no network calls of their own and work completely offline. Tynkr Inkpress makes one exception: during print PDF export, it downloads remote images linked from the web in your manuscript (use local images on your PC to avoid any connection); Inkpress also uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 (which includes SmartScreen) and Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome for print PDF export.
Q: Where are my files stored, and does Tynkr encrypt them?
A: Every Tynkr app stores your work in ordinary files on your own Windows PC — JSON, Markdown, EPUB, PDF, and HTML — and uninstalling an app leaves your data in place. Tynkr Ledger, Vault, Hearth, and Forge save in a folder you choose and offer optional password protection that encrypts your files on disk. Tynkr Inkpress saves preferences and default exports in Documents\Tynkr Inkpress plus a .inkpress.json sidecar next to each manuscript without encrypting them; those files are protected by your Windows account.

## App details and FAQs

### Tynkr Ledger
URL: https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/ledger/
What it is: Personal finance on your own disk: transactions, budgets, bills, debt payoff, net worth. Local-first Windows app — no cloud, no accounts, no subscription.
Platform: Windows · category: FinanceApplication · status: in development (not yet released); pay-once model (one-time purchase when it ships).
Q: Does Ledger connect to my bank?
A: No. Ledger never asks for bank credentials and makes no network requests to financial institutions. You import transactions by downloading a CSV, OFX or QFX file from your bank’s website and opening it in Ledger.
Q: Where is my financial data stored?
A: In JSON files in a folder you choose on your own machine — one file per year of transactions, plus files for budgets, bills, debts and settings. You can open, back up, or move them with any tool. If you turn on optional encryption, the files are encrypted with your password.
Q: Is there a subscription?
A: No. Ledger is a one-time purchase when it launches. Bug fixes are always free; major version upgrades are a separate purchase. There is no account and no recurring billing.
Q: Does it work offline?
A: Yes. The app needs no internet connection and makes no network calls of its own. Updates arrive through the Microsoft Store when you're online. Airplane mode is a supported configuration.
Q: Can I get my data out?
A: It was never locked in. Your data is already JSON on your disk (or encrypted JSON, if you turn encryption on), and you can back it all up as a single file anytime. If you stop using Ledger, your files keep working with anything that reads JSON.

### Tynkr Vault
URL: https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/vault/
What it is: Notes in plain Markdown files you own, with tasks, weekly reviews, and typo-tolerant search. Local-first Windows app — no cloud or subscription.
Platform: Windows · category: BusinessApplication · status: in development (not yet released); pay-once model (one-time purchase when it ships).
Q: Are my notes stored in a database?
A: No. Your notes are plain Markdown files in a folder you choose. Vault keeps a local search index for speed, but the files themselves are the source of truth — readable by any editor. If you turn on encryption, the files are encrypted on disk and Vault unlocks them with your password.
Q: Can I use Vault with an existing folder of Markdown files?
A: Yes — import them. Choose the .md files you want and Vault copies each one into your vault as a note, titled with its file name. Your original files aren’t moved or changed.
Q: How do I sync notes between machines?
A: However you like — the vault is just a folder, so any file sync you already trust works. Vault itself never syncs anything and never sends your notes anywhere.
Q: Is there a subscription?
A: No. Vault is a one-time purchase when it launches. Bug fixes are always free; major version upgrades are a separate purchase. No account, no recurring billing.
Q: Does it work offline?
A: Yes. The app needs no internet connection and makes no network calls of its own. Updates arrive through the Microsoft Store when you're online.

### Tynkr Hearth
URL: https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/hearth/
What it is: Map your home purchase on your own PC: mortgage math, loan comparison, cash-to-close, roadmap, and document checklist. Local-first Windows app.
Platform: Windows · category: BusinessApplication · status: in development (not yet released); pay-once model (one-time purchase when it ships).
Q: Is Hearth a mortgage lender or broker?
A: No. Hearth is planning software. It doesn’t sell loans, take referral fees, or send your information to lenders — it has no way to, since nothing leaves your machine.
Q: Where do my documents live?
A: Wherever you already keep them. Hearth doesn’t store your documents — it tracks a checklist of the eleven a purchase usually needs, with a status and a note for each. Your PDFs stay in your own folders.
Q: Are the mortgage numbers accurate?
A: The math is standard amortization plus the taxes, insurance, PMI, and fee figures you enter. It’s a planning estimate — your lender’s Loan Estimate is the binding document.
Q: Is there a subscription?
A: No. Hearth is a one-time purchase when it launches. Bug fixes are always free; major version upgrades are a separate purchase. No account, no recurring billing.
Q: What happens to my data after I close?
A: It stays yours. Your JSON files and property photos stay in your data folder as a record of the purchase — and you can export a .zip backup or CSVs any time.

### Tynkr Forge
URL: https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/forge/
What it is: Inventory, orders and invoicing for a small shop, with no monthly fee — one local-first Windows app. No cloud, no accounts, no subscription.
Features, in order: inventory with stock levels and reorder targets, vendors and purchase orders, customer CRM and sales pipeline, proposals, PDF invoices, projects and time tracking, financial dashboard, contracts, expenses with receipts, and reminders.
Platform: Windows · category: BusinessApplication · status: in development (not yet released); pay-once model (one-time purchase when it ships).
Q: Can Forge send invoices by email?
A: Forge generates the invoice as a PDF you send however you already email — it doesn’t send mail itself or route your client data through any server.
Q: Where does my business data live?
A: In flat JSON files on your disk — one per module — plus a vault folder where receipts and documents sit as ordinary files. Back it up with whatever you already use.
Q: Can multiple people use it?
A: Forge is built for solo owners and works on one machine at a time. Because the data is flat files, you can share the folder between machines with your own sync — but there’s no multi-user server, by design.
Q: Is there a subscription?
A: No. Forge is a one-time purchase when it launches. Bug fixes are always free; major version upgrades are a separate purchase. No account, no recurring billing.
Q: Does it work offline?
A: Yes. The app needs no internet connection and makes no network calls of its own. Updates arrive through the Microsoft Store when you're online.

### Tynkr Inkpress
URL: https://tynkr.builtbyjoshstudio.com/inkpress/
What it is: Format manuscripts into EPUB 3 ebooks, KDP paperback print PDFs, and author-site web pages with live previews. Local-first Windows desktop app.
Platform: Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later (x64) · category: DesignApplication · status: coming soon to the Microsoft Store; pay-once model (one-time purchase when it ships).
Q: Which manuscript formats can Inkpress open, and does it change my file?
A: Inkpress opens Word (.docx or .doc), Google Docs (.odt or .docx download), PDF, Markdown and plain-text files. Your original manuscript is never modified — when you save changes in your usual editor, Inkpress reloads the manuscript automatically, and saves each book's layout settings in a .inkpress.json sidecar file next to it.
Q: How does Inkpress handle privacy, internet access and SmartScreen?
A: Inkpress has no account, no telemetry and no analytics, and it sends nothing to us. The app's own code makes no network connections, with one exception: when you make a print PDF, any image your manuscript links to on the web is downloaded from the site that hosts it so it appears in the PDF (that site can see your IP address). The live preview loads nothing from the internet, and the EPUB leaves web images out — use images stored on your PC to avoid any connection. The window uses the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which sends diagnostic data to Microsoft under your Windows diagnostic-data settings and includes Microsoft Defender SmartScreen, and print PDF export runs Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome in the background under their own privacy terms.
Q: Where are my files stored, and are they encrypted?
A: Preferences, your recent-books list, the sample book and default exports stay in Documents\Tynkr Inkpress, and each book's settings live in a .inkpress.json file next to its manuscript. These are ordinary files protected by your Windows account — Inkpress does not encrypt them, and uninstalling Inkpress does not remove them.
Q: What are the Windows requirements?
A: Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later on 64-bit (x64) Windows, with a display that fits a 1100 × 720 window (English-language interface). The UI uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 (preinstalled on Windows 11 and most Windows 10 PCs), and print PDF export uses Microsoft Edge (included with Windows) or Google Chrome. Other export formats need no browser.
Q: Does Inkpress write, edit, or build full paperback cover wraps?
A: No. Inkpress lays out your book — it does not write, edit or proofread your prose, and it does not create full wraparound paperback covers. It can generate a typographic ebook cover from your title and author (or use your own JPG, PNG or SVG cover), and gives you estimated page count, spine width and inside gutter while you format. Always check the final print PDF in KDP's own previewer before publishing.
Q: Is there a subscription or in-app upgrade?
A: No. Tynkr Inkpress is coming soon to the Microsoft Store as a one-time purchase with every edition, font pairing, border option and export format included. There are no in-app purchases, no license keys to enter and no recurring billing; updates arrive through the Microsoft Store.

## Shared contract

- On your machine: Ledger, Vault, Hearth and Forge keep flat files in a folder you choose; Inkpress keeps preferences and default exports in Documents\Tynkr Inkpress plus a .inkpress.json sidecar next to each manuscript.
- No cloud, no accounts, no subscriptions, no telemetry: none of the apps send us your data. Ledger, Vault, Hearth and Forge make no network calls of their own; Inkpress only downloads remote web images linked in a manuscript during print PDF export (plus WebView2 diagnostic data/SmartScreen and Edge or Chrome for PDF export). Microsoft handles the purchase, license, and updates through the Microsoft Store.
- Pay-once model (one-time purchase per app when released); every app will be certified, signed, and delivered by the Microsoft Store, with updates through the Store automatically.
- Publisher: Built by Josh Studio LLC (Tynkr Tools & Co brand); support: support@builtbyjoshstudio.com.
